title: Non-explosion of Brownian Fleming–Viot systems in arbitrary domains
decision_reason: Source-backed fingerprint, independently authored corroboration, ten theorem-scope comparisons and separated A61 self-review passed; rendering and bibliography checks passed. No unresolved material status conflict located.

problem_fingerprint.objects: For every d>=2, every nonempty bounded connected open D in R^d, every integer N>=3, and every initial configuration x in D^N, a fixed-size Brownian Fleming–Viot system.
problem_fingerprint.motion: Between resampling times each labelled particle moves as an independent standard Brownian motion, with generator (1/2)Delta, until first exit from D. There is no drift or reflection.
problem_fingerprint.resampling: At a boundary hit, the exiting particle instantaneously moves to the current position of one uniformly chosen other particle. The remaining particles are unchanged; future Brownian increments and the uniform choices use the usual independent construction.
problem_fingerprint.initial_conditions: Every deterministic interior configuration is allowed, including coincident positions. Boundary initial points are not included.
problem_fingerprint.target: If tau_k is the kth resampling time and tau_infinity=lim_k tau_k, is P_x(tau_infinity=infinity)=1 for every such d,D,N,x? Equivalently, finitely many resampling events in each finite time interval.
problem_fingerprint.scope: No boundary regularity, Lipschitz, cone or interior-ball condition is assumed. N=2 is already solved and is stated as progress. N is fixed in each system; no large-N, stationary or genealogical limiting assertion is requested.
problem_fingerprint.family_policy: One Brownian non-explosion family; dimensions, particle counts, regular-domain cases and equivalent jump-time formulations are not separate entries.

independent_corroboration: Burdzy supplies the explicit bounded-domain problem. Independently authored Kwaśnicki retains the more-than-two-particle question. Revisions and mirrors are not independent works.

resolution_comparisons.comparison: The statement matches a broader domain class, but its proof has an acknowledged error. BBF12 Example 5.3, BBP12 §1, K24 Remark 1.2 and B-open explicitly explain why this is not an established general solution.
The result covers every Brownian starting configuration, but only two particles. The candidate starts at N=3.
The Lipschitz constant must be below c(N,d). Its large-N limit is 1/sqrt(d-1); the theorem does not remove the geometric restriction or cover every fixed N on arbitrary domains.
The polyhedral-domain theorem concerns two particles; particle number cannot be increased without another argument.

resolution_comparisons.locator: 2009 author manuscript Definitions 1–2, Theorem 1 and Proposition 2.
resolution_comparisons.comparison: Requires a regular boundary-distance function with bounded derivatives and nonvanishing gradient, plus a sufficiently large particle count. Arbitrary rough domains do not satisfy these assumptions.
Negative-dimensional Bessel extinction and the all-N example use singular drift. The latter also reflects at 2. Neither matches drift-free Brownian motion killed at every part of the boundary.
The convergence theorem presupposes non-explosion of each approximating system. Approximation of the killed process by regular domains does not establish the target for the original fixed-N dynamics.
Uniform resampling meets the relocation condition, but C2 boundary distance in a collar, or a suitable regular substitute, remains required. The candidate assumes no such function.
Uniform mixing and approximation estimates are obtained for C2 domains with a smooth gradient potential and metastability conditions. These do not imply rough-domain non-explosion.

Ergodicity and the stationary Dirichlet-eigenfunction approximation use the specified regular Lipschitz class. They justify the application connection without solving fixed-N existence for arbitrary D.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Non-explosion follows under Hypotheses 1–2, including a C^2 boundary-distance function with uniformly bounded derivatives in a fixed boundary neighbourhood.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: This repeats a regular-boundary sufficient criterion and does not address all bounded connected open domains.

nearest_existing_entries.comparison: Rate-one binary branching on the whole line with removal of a leftmost particle; the target is large-N ancestry on a logarithmic clock. Here branching is triggered by domain exit, cloning is uniform and the target is fixed-N non-explosion.

Discrete population-count mass-action jump chains with weakly reversible reaction graphs, arbitrary reaction order and a recurrence conclusion; neither state space nor jump rule matches Brownian boundary resampling.
An infection process on a nonamenable graph and a gap between global and local survival thresholds; no fixed finite Brownian population or boundary-exit construction.

normalization_checks: D is bounded, connected, nonempty and open; d>=2. Its boundary has no additional geometric regularity.
N>=3 is fixed in each system; no hidden limit or sufficiently-large-N qualification.
Brownian generator is (1/2)Delta; no drift, reflection, soft killing or alternative cloning weights.
Every deterministic interior initial configuration is included, also with coincident positions.
Uniform choice is among the N-1 surviving particles; conditional future Brownian increments are independent.
The accumulating event count, not the population size, can explode. Finite events on every bounded time interval is equivalent to tau_infinity=infinity.
All particle counts, dimensions and equivalent event-time formulations comprise one family.
